chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu al-Maghra', from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, from Salim al-Ashall, that he heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:

'Indeed, God Mighty and Majestic included the two parents alongside all other heirs of the inheritances, and did not reduce anything from the sixth for them; and He included the husband and wife, and did not reduce anything from the quarter and the eighth for them.'

key_terms.الثُّمُنُ: The eighth (1/8), the minimum guaranteed share for a wife when the deceased has children
key_terms.الرُّبُعُ: The quarter (1/4), the minimum guaranteed share for a husband when the deceased has no children
key_terms.السُّدُسُ: The sixth (1/6), the minimum guaranteed share for each parent when the deceased has children
key_terms.الْمَوَارِيثُ: Inheritances, the body of law concerning distribution of a deceased person's estate
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a common divine epithet indicating God's power and majesty

ai.seo_question: What are the minimum inheritance shares of parents and spouses in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a foundational principle of Shia inheritance law: the shares of parents and spouses are protected minimums — no matter how many other heirs are present, the parents will always receive at least one-sixth each (when the deceased has children), and the spouse will always receive at least one-quarter (husband, no children) or one-eighth (wife, with children). This doctrine addresses the issue of 'awl (reduction/deficiency) in inheritance where shares would theoretically exceed the estate, affirming that these minimum shares cannot be reduced.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Abu Al Magra, from Ibrahim Bin Maymoun, from Saalim Al Ashal, 
(The narrator) who heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Included the two parents upon the entirety of deserving inheritors. So He<sup>azwj</sup> did not Reduce anything from the sixth for the two of them, and Included the husband and the wife, so He<sup>azwj</sup> did not Reduce anything from the quarter and the eight for the two of them, (respectively)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ’Udhaynah who has said that Zurarah has said, the following: “If you wish to deal with deficiency it is compensated from the share of those who have more, like children and brothers from the father.
The husband and brothers from the mother do not compensate the deficiency from their ordained shares which Allah has mentioned.’”
